1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O Nxe4 5.background: Once common: Emanuel Lasker played it several times, including three games of the 1908 World Championship match, before it declined in popularity.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O Nxe4 5.strategy: Attacks the loose knight on e4 and protects the bishop on b5 in one move, so Black has to decide where the knight goes. White is set to regain the pawn and keeps the initiative while Black untangles.

Regains the pawn at once by capturing on e5, which trades the central tension for a half-open d-file. It gives Black time to castle with an active knight on e4, so White gets a solid, unambitious game rather than an initiative.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O Nxe4 5.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence, Minckwitz Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O Nxe4 5.strategy: Retreats the knight with a threat on the bishop. After the exchange on c6 Black has doubled pawns but the two bishops and active pieces, enough compensation for the pawn White regains on e5.

Backs up the knight on e4 with a pawn, but clears d7 so the bishop pins the knight on c6 to the king. With e5 attacked twice and its only defender pinned, the pawn is in trouble: the centre is overextended.
